column1: # Corana et al. (1987) protocol-replication reference table.
# Source (the ONLY permitted source for the numbers below):
#   A. Corana, M. Marchesi, C. Martini, S. Ridella,
#   "Minimizing multimodal functions of continuous variables with the
#   'simulated annealing' algorithm", ACM TOMS 13(3), 262-280 (1987),
#   doi:10.1145/29380.29864 -- INCLUDING its published Corrigenda.
# This file ships EMPTY (header only).  While it has no data rows,
# test_anneal_corana_protocol.cpp reports itself as SKIPPED.  Fill it by
# transcribing the paper's experimental setup and result tables -- never
# from memory, never from secondary sources.  While transcribing, also
# verify the test-function definitions coded in
# test_anneal_corana_protocol.cpp (paraboloid / Rosenbrock / staircase
# and the weight cycle d = {1, 1000, 10, 100}) against the paper and
# correct them there if they differ.
# Columns (tab-separated; one row per paper run):
#   function  paraboloid | rosenbrock | staircase
#   dim       problem dimension used in the paper run (2, 4, 10, ...)
#   low,high  uniform search bounds of the paper run (scalars)
#   start     starting point: comma-separated list (dim values) or one
#             value replicated across dimensions
#   v0        paper's initial step size (absolute, original units);
#             "-" = implementation default
#   t_init    paper's starting temperature T0 for the run
#   rt        temperature reduction coefficient r_T
#   ns        step-adjustment cycle length N_S
#   nt        temperature-step length N_T (loops per temperature)
#   neps      termination window N_eps
#   eps       termination tolerance epsilon
#   accuracy  "reached the optimum" gate on the final best f (from the
#             final-function-value column of the paper's tables)
#   neval     paper's reported number of function evaluations for SA on
#             this run (mean, if the paper reports several sequences)
# Acceptance policy applied by the test (fixed in code, not here):
#   20/20 fixed seeds end with best f <= accuracy, and the mean eval
#   count over the 20 seeds lies within [0.5x, 2x] of neval.
